title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X → S smooth, S of characteristic p. Relative Frobenius F_{X/S}: X → X^{(p/S)} = X', composed with the projection X' → X (the diagram in the top-left corner over S → S). Cartier operator C: Z^1_{X/S} → Ω^1_{X'/S}. The 'Convention' fixes where F*_{X/S}(Cω) lives: in Γ F*Ω^1_{X'/S} ≅ Γ(Ω^1_{X/S})^{(p)}, the Frobenius twist. That twist maps to p-th tensor (really symmetric) powers by ω ↦ ω^{⊗p}, with ⟨ω^{⊗p}, ξ^{⊗p}⟩ = ω(ξ)^p.

Key formula. Change a connection (on a line bundle, or on an object of the same type) by a closed 1-form ω. The invariant v (from the context, the p-curvature or a p-curvature-type obstruction) then changes as
 v'(ξ) = v(ξ) + ω(ξ)^p − (F*Cω)(ξ),
intrinsically v' = v + (ω^{⊗p} − F*Cω) = v + F*_{X/S}(ω̃ − Cω). Here ω̃ is the base-changed form in Ω^1_{X'}. This is Katz's/Cartier's formula: the p-curvature of d+ω, for ω closed, is F*(ω' − Cω).

Consequence. The class of v, for L with all its connections allowed to vary, lives in Γ(X, Ω^{1⊗p}) / Im[γ: Z^1(X, Ω^•_{X/S}) → Γ(X, Ω^{1⊗p})], where γ(ω) = ω^{⊗p} − F*Cω. Its vanishing means L has a connection with zero p-curvature, i.e. by Cartier descent L ≅ F*L'.

Page numbered '2' (globalisation). For X proper over S, localising on S, he gets a morphism of sheaves
 (Φ) Pic (of line bundles admitting an integrable connection: 'Pic ⇒ Pic conn. int.') → Coker[f_*Z^1_{X/S} →γ f_*(Ω^{1⊗p}_{X/S})],
with f_*Z^1 = Ker[d^1: f_*Ω^1 → f_*Ω^2]. The circled marginal note 'pas linéaire!' stresses that γ is additive but not O_S-linear: it mixes the p-linear Frobenius part with the p^{-1}-linear Cartier part.

Hypotheses for representability of the target:
 a) Ω^1, Ω^2, Ω^{1⊗p} are cohomologically flat over S in dimension 0;
 b) Coker d^1 and Im d^1 are flat over S (automatic for relative dimension 1, where Ω^2 = 0);
 c) Ker γ is flat over S.
Under these, he claims the target of Φ is representable by a vector bundle (the sentence breaks off).

Purpose: the Artin–Milne/Illusie exact sequence 0 → O*_{X'} → F_*O*_X → F_*Z^1 →(W−C) Ω^1_{X'} → 0, read through p-curvature. The aim is a relative-moduli invariant measuring the failure of a line bundle to be a Frobenius pullback, in the Gauss–Manin/Cartier setting of this folder.
errors: ω ↦ ω^{⊗p} is not additive into the tensor power; the correct target is the Frobenius twist (Ω^1)^{(p)}, or Sym^p. Only the pairing with ξ^{⊗p}, giving ω(ξ)^p, is meaningful as written.

The claim that the cokernel of the non-linear additive map γ is 'représentable par un fibré vectoriel' is doubtful as stated. Cokernels of p-linear/p^{-1}-linear additive maps of vector bundles are in general commutative group schemes, or even zero as fppf sheaves (e.g. x ↦ x^p − x on G_a), not vector bundles. The topology and the precise sense of representability are left unspecified, and the sentence is unfinished.
The domain of Φ is ambiguous: as written it is Pic, but the construction only makes sense on line bundles admitting an integrable connection (or on Pic^♮ modulo connections).

ideas.what: Change of p-curvature under ∇ ↦ ∇+ω for closed ω: Δψ = F*(ω̃ − Cω) = ω^p − F*Cω
ideas.modern_name: Katz's p-curvature formula for rank-one connections / Cartier operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz (Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem, 1970), after Cartier

ideas.what: Obstruction for a line bundle to be a Frobenius pullback, valued in Γ(Ω^{1(p)}) / Im(W − C on closed forms)
ideas.modern_name: Cartier descent obstruction; Artin–Milne exact sequence O*/O*^p → Z^1 →(W−C) Ω^1_{X'}

ideas.what: Relative globalisation: a map from the relative Picard functor (bundles admitting connections) to the cokernel of the non-linear additive map γ: f_*Z^1 → f_*Ω^{1⊗p}, with flatness conditions for representability
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one p-curvature (Hitchin-type) map on Pic^♮_{X/S}; Pic^♮ as torsor in characteristic p

missed.claim: An attempt at a relative, representable 'p-curvature class' invariant on the Picard functor of a proper smooth X/S in characteristic p. Flatness hypotheses a)–c) are set out to make the target, the cokernel of a non-linear additive map, representable; the conclusion is left unfinished and is probably not correct as stated.
missed.quote: Alors le 2e membre de (Φ) est représentable par un fibré vectoriel
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as historical evidence: around 1972 Grothendieck was considering moduli-level p-curvature maps for rank-one connections. These anticipate in spirit the rank-one Hitchin map in characteristic p, but the content is now standard (Bezrukavnikov–Braverman, Ogus–Vologodsky).

deep.surprise_reason: The local formula is Katz's well-known p-curvature/Cartier formula. The globalisation to a map from Pic to a cokernel sheaf is a natural, unfinished sketch whose representability claim is shaky. Of historical interest only, with no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'de ch. plats sur S en dim 0' should read 'cohomologiquement plats sur S en dimension 0' (EGA III §7 terminology).
'Pic ⇒ Pic conn. inf.' is probably 'Pic conn. int.' (line bundles with integrable connection), or the subfunctor of Pic of bundles admitting a connection.
The top-left diagram is X →F_{X/S}→ X^{(p/S)} → X over S → S (Frobenius of S), not two separate lines.
The circled marginal note reads 'pas linéaire!' and refers to the map γ.
